expenditures.detail: TWO discrepancies, both traced, nothing nudged. (1) PDF p3 CLOSES EXACTLY: its 17 rows sum 75.00+0.99+71.40+41.00+13.85+55.00+18.48+233.39+126.05+108.58+15.99+41.80+24.70+29.01+306.59+14.92+70.00 = 1,246.75 = its printed subtotal to the cent. (2) PDF p4 does NOT: its 14 rows sum 351.70+106.17+1000.00+1200.00+60.00+360.00+150.00+1000.00+235.00+647.22+100.00+2756.33+735.00+218.28 = 8,919.70 against a printed page subtotal of 8,819.70 — the rows exceed the filer's own subtotal by EXACTLY 100.00. Direction matters: a shortfall could be a missed row (the §H3 two-entries-in-one-band trap), but a SURPLUS cannot be, and the band crops confirm it independently — the amount-column scan returned a clean 17-rule ladder with no doubled band, the first-entry control put line 1 on band 1, and the one-past-the-end control rendered empty. Two candidate explanations were weighed: (a) the filer's subtotal omitted line 11, 'Linda Housekeeper (Table) 100' — the ONLY row on the page whose value is exactly 100.00 — or (b) line 13 is 635.00 rather than the 735.00 read here. (b) was tested by the §H6 method, comparing the disputed leading digit against this same filer's own glyphs on the page that DID close exactly: his confirmed '7' (p3 lines 1, 3, 17) is a flat top bar with a diagonal descender and his confirmed '6' (p3 line 9, 126.05) is a closed loop with a curved ascender; line 13's leading digit is unmistakably the '7' form. That rules (b) out and leaves (a) as the unique row-level attribution — so the delta is RETAINED VERBATIM, every figure is as printed, and the filer's own subtotal is left as he wrote it. (3) SEPARATELY, the printed GRAND total 11,561.14 does not equal the sum of the two printed page subtotals (1,246.75 + 8,819.70 = 10,066.45), nor of the rows as transcribed (1,246.75 + 8,919.70 = 10,166.45); it exceeds them by 1,494.69 and 1,394.69 respectively. Nothing in the retained document accounts for the difference, and no row or combination of rows attributes it. Every Page/of foliation box on all three schedule sheets is BLANK, so foliation gives no evidence either way as to whether a further Schedule B sheet existed and was not published. Recorded as a fact about the document, not adjudicated, and NOT used to synthesize any figure.

escalation_note: Every one of the 14 amount cells on PDF p4 was escalated to a 1000 dpi tight --value crop, because the page does not close on its own subtotal and the surplus had to be attributed rather than asserted. All fourteen reproduced exactly as read at 200 dpi (351.70 / 106.17 / 1,000.00 / 1,200 / 60 / 360 / 150 / 1,000 / 235 / 647.22 / 100 / 2,756.33 / 7,35-00 / 218.28), so no misreading explains the +100.00 and the delta is the document's own. Four further escalations: the p2 line-3 amount at 1200 dpi (settling '$ 5000' against a possible 500.00 — the closure decides it), the p3 and p4 subtotal/total lines at 900 dpi (1,246.75 with a bare DASH on p3's total line; 8,819.70 and 11,561.14 on p4), and the p4 line-13 date and amount at 1400 dpi. THE ONE FIGURE STILL FLAGGED is p4 line 13: the cell prints what reads as '7,35' with raised cents '00'. The digits are unambiguous at 1400 dpi and the leading digit matches this filer's confirmed '7' rather than his confirmed '6' (see recon), so 735.00 is recorded — but the comma sits where a thousands separator would go, which no reading of the cell makes sensible, and the row is flagged needs_review=1 rather than repaired. Its date's final digit is likewise imperfectly formed (2016 vs 2015); recorded as read with the doubt stated, never resolved from the report date.

The `--col 82,94` amount-column scan gives the correct ladder, ~+0.4 pct lower: 20.69 / 24.75 / 28.66 / 32.55 / 36.39 / 40.43 / 44.34 / 48.30 / 52.18 / 56.11 / 60.07 / 63.98 / 67.84 / 71.82 / 75.75 / 79.68 / 83.59, pitch 3.93, 17 rules = 17 lines (§H1), with row 1 extrapolated one pitch up to 16.76. THREE-CROP PROOF at 900 dpi --value on the bands stored here: row 1 rendered the printed 'Amount' header over '$ 500-00' (first-entry control — the filer did not skip line 1); row 5 pct:82.0,32.55,16.0,3.84@p2 rendered '$ 1,000' with line 4's own '$1,000' cleanly ABOVE the top rule; and the §B5 one-past-the-end control on band 6 rendered EMPTY (line 5's figure sitting above the band, nothing below it). The stored `cell` [82.00,98.00] is much WIDER than the printed amount column [82.58,92.46] because this filer's raised cents run past the printed rule (§G2): bounded by the printed band, the row-1 crop lost the raised '00' of $500-00 entirely. Report type 'Seven days preceding the General Election'; the SIGNATURE DATE BOX IS BLANK (signed, undated); the clerk's red received stamp reads '8:52 10-30-2018' with initials. THE AMENDMENT QUESTION IS AN HONEST BLANK — on this blank the two options are printed as CIRCLES rather than boxes and NEITHER is marked; nothing was inferred. FORM STOCK: this is the OLD 'county-only' blank — the eagle seal, the title 'FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN REPORT FOR COUNTY CANDIDATES', and the citation 'Utah County Code 2-5-2 & Utah State Code 17-16-6.5' — still in circulation in OCTOBER 2018, alongside the genuinely-2018-strap-lined stock used by two other filers in this same chunk and the leftover 2016 stock used by a third. That is the §A4/§C1 point in its strongest form: template vintage orders nothing in time. Its three inner sheets carry NO year strapline at all, and Schedule B REUSES Schedule A's headings, printing 'Name of Contributor' over the payee column with no Purpose column. THIS FILING HAS NO SUMMARY PAGE: the four pages are cover / Schedule A / Schedule B / Schedule B, so there is no Column A, no Column B, no balance ladder and no cover cross-check — each side was gated on the schedules' own printed footers and nothing was synthesized (§E5/§F6). ⚠ SCOPE — READ BEFORE SUMMING: the ledgers plainly restate more than one reporting period, and on Schedule B more than one CYCLE (rows dated 2015, 2016 and 2017 sit above the 2018 rows). The utah regime promotes a per-period figure; these totals are not one. With no summary page there is no Column A/B pair to test the scope against, so the §A6 `cumulative-exact` label does not apply either — the honest statement is that the printed totals close on their own rows and their scope is the filer's, not the period's. FOLIATION: every Page/of box on all three schedule sheets is BLANK — a ninth practice for the running tally, and the reason the grand-total discrepancy cannot be resolved for or against a missing sheet. ROW-INDEX TRAPS SCREENED: on all three schedules the first written entry is band 1 (crop-proved on each), there is no banner, voided or continuation line, the one-past-the-end control rendered the printed subtotal on pp2-3 and an empty band on p4, and the amount-column scans returned clean 17-rule ladders with no doubled band. GEOMETRY HAZARD WORTH CARRYING FORWARD: pp2-3 are skewed +1.0 deg and the FULL-WIDTH rule list is off by roughly half a row in the amount column — a first attempt using it put a figure at the edge of the wrong band; the `--col` amount-column recovery is mandatory on this filing. FIELD-SHIFT SCREEN: columns assigned by CONTENT against the printed headings; two names overrun their column into the address column and one payee cell carries two names on two lines, but nothing is inverted and every column remains assignable. PRIVACY: this filing is NOT redacted; no donor or vendor street address is printed anywhere on it (the address column is blank on all 31 expenditure rows and on three of the five contribution rows), the two contribution rows that carry an address carry a CITY NAME ONLY, and nothing beyond city/state was carried into any field or note.
